Display timezone changes the readable date, not the underlying instant or timestamp.

Dates without guesswork

ISO input requires a timezone: use Z for UTC or an offset such as +05:30. Unix input requires you to choose seconds or milliseconds. Calendar input uses your device timezone.

During a daylight saving fall-back, a local time can occur twice. Use an ISO timestamp with an explicit offset to identify the intended instant. Nonexistent local times during a spring-forward transition are rejected.

ISO and Unix outputs refer to the same instant. The selected display timezone applies only to the readable date and time. Unix seconds are rounded down when milliseconds are present.
